i0: The **future continuous** (*will be doing*) describes an action **in progress** at a time in the future: *This time tomorrow I**'ll be lying** on a beach.*
i1: The **future perfect** (*will have done*) describes an action that will be **complete** before a time in the future: *By June I**'ll have finished** my course.* For assumptions like *He'll be sleeping now*, see [Modals of Deduction](/blog/grammar/modals-of-deduction/#md-will-assumption).
fcp-continuous.s: **will be + -ing** for an action in progress at a particular time in the future: *At 8 tonight I'll be watching the match.*
fcp-continuous.b1: The future continuous puts you **in the middle** of a future action: *Don't call at 9. I**'ll be having** dinner.* (I'll start before 9 and finish after.)
fcp-continuous.b2: Typical time phrases: *this time tomorrow / next week, at 6 o'clock tomorrow, all day tomorrow, when you arrive*.
fcp-continuous.b3: Compare with the past continuous, which does the same for the past: *At 8 last night I **was watching** TV.* See [Past Continuous](/blog/grammar/past-continuous/).
x.fcp-continuous-s01: In progress at a future time: *will be lying*.
x.fcp-continuous-s03: In progress at a future time: *will be sitting*.
